slot.brief: Given the mean of n observations, find the new mean after each observation is scaled and shifted (axᵢ + b).

stem: The mean of $25$ observations is $40$. If each observation is multiplied by $3$ and then decreased by $12$, the new mean is
working:
Let the original observations be $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{25}$ with mean $\bar{x} = 40$.
Each new observation $y_i$ is obtained by the linear transformation:
$$y_i = 3x_i - 12$$

The new mean $\bar{y}$ is given by:
$$\bar{y} = \dfrac{1}{25}\sum_{i=1}^{25} y_i = \dfrac{1}{25}\sum_{i=1}^{25}(3x_i - 12)$$
$$\bar{y} = 3\left(\dfrac{1}{25}\sum_{i=1}^{25} x_i\right) - 12 = 3\bar{x} - 12$$
$$\bar{y} = 3(40) - 12 = 120 - 12 = 108$$

Independent check: Mean transforms linearly: new mean = 3×40 − 12 = 120 − 12 = 108.
